name: Scanned Workflow
description: The run considered this workflow, and the outcome says what actually happened to it. This edge exists so that absence means something: a workflow with no SCANNED_WORKFLOW edge from the current run was NOT observed by this scanner, which is a different fact from a workflow that was scanned and found clean. Coverage is the property that keeps a findings view from rendering silence as safety.

property_schema.description: What became of this workflow on this run. Every non-evaluated outcome must say why in `reason` — an unexplained `skipped` is the shape that lets a coverage gap read as a clean result.

outcome.description: `evaluated`: the scanner read the file and its findings (possibly none) are on the grid. `parse-failed`: the file was materialized but the scanner could not parse it, so this workflow's findings are UNKNOWN, not zero. `skipped`: the collector refused the row before scanning (a path that failed sanitizing, a cap). `no-yaml`: github_core collected the workflow but captured no `raw_yaml` for it, so there was nothing to scan — the most common non-evaluated state on a real grid (40 of 117 workflows, observed 2026-09-10) and the one most likely to be misread as clean.

reason.description: Why the outcome is not `evaluated`, in terms a reader can act on: the parser error, the sanitizing rule that refused the path, or the absence that left nothing to read.
